HTTP Status Code

You might say

The page opens to a 404 error. Did I write the wrong link, or was the deployment incomplete?

A three-digit answer from the server about a request: success, redirect, a request problem, or a server failure·When a page fails, a 404 response says the target resource was not found; check the URL, route, and deployment. A 500 is a server-error-class response; correlate its request ID with server logs to find clues. A status code points to the next check but does not prove the root cause or responsibility on its own.

example.com/save
GET/old-page404The server has no such resource
POST/save500The server failed while handling it
GET/dashboard401The identity was not accepted
GET/home200This request succeeded
500 · The server failed while handling itServer

Check server logs for this request; the page message cannot replace the status code

Use the buttons above to switch status-code scenarios. The first digit groups the outcome (2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error); the exact number narrows the cause.

How status codes guide where to look

Read the category first: The first digit groups response classes: 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error, and 5xx server error. This guides the next check; use the request and logs to locate a cause.

The exact number narrows the cause: A 404 response says the target resource was not found, 401 means valid authentication credentials are missing, and 400 signals a problem with the request. Check the URL, request, and response for the cause.

Where to find it: The browser Network panel records the status code of every request; debugging tools and errors reported by AI agents also print the number directly.

What it does not tell you

A status code describes the request outcome, not whether the code has bugs. A 200 also does not prove the business result: a save endpoint can return success while nothing was written, so acceptance still depends on the business outcome.
